findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default, risking exposure of sensitive report data at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket ACL / public access control
findings.description: No acl attribute is specified, meaning the bucket relies on the AWS default (private) but there is also no explicit public access block configuration shown, and combined with force_destroy=true and no encryption, sensitive report data has weak protection and could be at risk if bucket policies elsewhere are permissive.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving financial ledger export data unencrypted at rest, which is a serious exposure risk for sensitive financial records.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket storing model artifacts, so data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving operational runbook content (potentially containing sensitive operational/credential details) unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL; if Terraform accepts this literally it likely fails, but if it maps to or is intended as a write-enabling ACL for log delivery, granting overly broad write access to the audit trail bucket undermines the integrity of audit logs. This should be explicitly set to 'log-delivery-write' with careful scoping or use bucket policy instead of ACL.

The uploaded object does not specify server-side encryption (kms_key_id or server_side_encryption), and it is placed into aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive which itself lacks default encryption, so the vendor-roster.xlsx file is stored unencrypted.
